blocks.text: To order something from a catalog or a magazine, you can use an **Order** **Form**. Be sure to include all the information about the item and where to send it.
blocks.features: 'Order' and 'Form' are bold single words within the sentence.
Handwritten/script responses follow in the fields below; 'Please print clearly' is a print instruction, not a response.

blocks.features: 'Washington Jr. High' is a handwritten (script) response.

print.notes: The form fields are enclosed in BANA box lines in the actual braille (6.7.3c) — neither run recorded this; recovered directly from the source text (a full-width row of dot-2356 before the fields, dot-12356 after). Several handwritten/typed 'response' fields are wrapped in UEB script indicators in the real braille (6.7.3g, this sample's own illustrated rule) — Emboss's typeform model (engine/louis.mjs TYPEFORM: italic/underline/bold only) has no script indicator at all, so these are built as plain text and the mismatch on every such field is expected (F-169, which explicitly names 6.7.3g). Both A and B also invented specific address/teacher/room field values ('Address 248 Greenwood', 'Teacher Mrs. Lee Grade 6 Room 8', etc. — B only) where the book's own braille excerpt shows nothing but an ellipsis (444) — there is no print evidence for any such fields, and they are not included here.

uncertain: 'Book Title (Please print clearly)': the exact capitalisation/typeform of '(please print clearly)' is not fully resolved — forward-translating '(PLEASE PRINT CLEARLY)' as a genuine all-caps passage does not reproduce the agreed braille's exact indicator placement (the passage-caps close marker sits BEFORE the closing parenthesis in the agreed braille, but AFTER it in Emboss's own output for that exact input, in isolation or with trailing context); liblouis back-translation instead suggests title case ('Please print clearly'). Not investigated further since this field's own script/box wrapping is already not representable (F-169) regardless of this residual capitalisation question.
resolution: B correctly excludes the running-head lines and gets 'McHenry, IL 65051'/'March 6, 2001'/'Amount' right where A has 'McHenry, IL 60051'/'March 6, 2011'/'Amt' — all three of A's readings are wrong, confirmed by liblouis back-translation of the agreed braille (engine/louis.mjs backTranslate) and cross-checked by exact forward-translation round trips. B, however, invents an entire set of address/teacher/room field values with no support in the braille (which shows only an ellipsis, 444, at that point) — exactly the fabrication risk the task instructions warn about; those invented fields are dropped here, not kept as 'B's version'. Neither run recorded the box lines present in the raw source (7...7 / g...g rows bracketing the form fields, confirmed directly in source-6.txt) or the 6.7.3g script-indicator wrapping on the handwritten response fields (both are F-169). print.blocks[2] was restructured from a single multi-line text blob into a boxed sequence of one paragraph per field, the most faithful representation this schema allows.
